Subject: Post-call: FinSecure deployment needs & data isolation (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today, Alex — really helpful to understand the use case. Quick written recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap of needs:
- Primary workload: document classification + PII redaction for customer support workflows (low-latency, ~100 reqs/s at peak).
- Data sensitivity: contains customer PII (SSNs, DOBs, payment tokens) and some financial documents.
- Compliance: must meet SOC 2 controls and provide audit evidence; procurement also asked about data residency and egress policies.
- Key ask: clarify whether Hosted API / Redwood Dedicated / Private VPC is required for "full" data isolation and what the tradeoffs are.

Clarifying questions:
1) Do inference requests need to originate and terminate inside FinSecure network (no egress ever)?
2) Is customer-managed KMS required for encryption-at-rest?
3) Who on your side would join a security/infra deep-dive (security architect + procurement?)

Short answers from our side (high-level):
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding but not suitable if you require customer-managed networking or strict no-egress requirements.
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools and logical data isolation; good for predictable throughput and often sufficient if contractual controls and encryption/KMS are acceptable.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): provides customer-managed networking, optional on-prem package, and the strongest isolation (no shared network egress under your control).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send our SOC 2 summary and a one-pager on Private deployment (attached).
- Can we schedule a 45-min security/infra call next week to go through connectivity/KMS details? Tuesday or Thursday are our best options.
- If procurement wants formal language, we can draft a short statement on data handling for the SOW.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, private_deployment_onepager.pdf

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call: FinSecure deployment needs & data isolation (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Internal notes / suggested language for Alex: 

- Data co-mingling: Redwood Dedicated provides logical isolation at the tenancy level; models/weights are shared per architecture but customer request/response data is stored encrypted and segregated by tenant ID. We can include contractual commitments for retention and deletion windows and provide audit logs. Suggested phrase: "Redwood will segregate Customer Data on a per-tenant basis and will not use Customer Data to train models or otherwise re-purpose data; data retention and deletion policies will be described in the SOW."

- Network / egress: Dedicated runs in Redwood-managed infrastructure and typically requires outbound connectivity to Redwood control plane endpoints for metrics/metrics, rollout, and billing. However, we support Private VPC deployments where inference instances are provisioned in the customer's VPC (no shared public egress), and we can provide an on-prem option for fully air-gapped environments. If customer requires "no egress" we should propose Private VPC or on-prem.

- KMS: Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments and is available for Dedicated via customer-managed keys in supported cloud providers (we'll need to confirm specific key types/providers in the security call).

- Next step: Recommend scheduling a security/infra call with our Solutions Engineer (Priya Natarajan) and our Security PM. I can join if needed.

I’ll draft suggested procurement language and a short slide for the memo.

-Rishi

Hi Alex — answering directly to help your procurement and security teams triage: 

1) Data co-mingling / retention: We will segregate customer data per-tenant and do not use request/response data to train models. We can commit to a retention and deletion window in the SOW (suggest 30/90/365 options) and provide audit logs showing deletion. Procurement language preview: "Redwood will segregate Customer Data on a per-tenant basis and will only retain data as defined in the SOW; Redwood will not use Customer Data to train models or for other product development purposes without explicit written consent."

2) Network / egress: If FinSecure requires inference traffic to remain fully inside your VPC with no external egress, Private (VPC) or on-prem is the right path. Redwood Dedicated provides logical isolation but runs in our managed fleet and requires connectivity to Redwood control plane endpoints for management/monitoring — we can minimize egress and offer strict allowlists, but we cannot guarantee zero egress on Dedicated.

3) KMS: Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments. We also support customer-managed keys for Dedicated in most major cloud providers; we'll confirm exact provider support on the call.
